Toy stochastic character map of biogeographic ranges of the toy backbone phylogeny

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_simmap_ranges.Rd

Stochastic character map (simmap) of phylograftR::toy_backbone with four states that are biogeographic ranges coded as in BioGeoBEARS: "A", "B", "AB" and "BC" (areas A, B and C; the area C is only found in "BC"). It can be used as simmap with treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE to graft taxa on branches in ranges that contain their allowed ranges (see the Details section "Biogeographic ranges as states" of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() and the examples of phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges).

It was simulated with phytools::sim.history() from a root in range "AB", with equal rates (0.04 per unit of time) for the anagenetic changes of range that gain or lose a single area ("A" <-> "AB", "B" <-> "AB" and "B" <-> "BC"). A change of two areas at once ("AB" <-> "BC") is not allowed. As a simulated history only has anagenetic changes, some of them were then moved to the parental node of their branch, to also represent cladogenetic events (see the Details section). Among the first 20000 seeds, the one used (3598) is the first giving a balanced map:

  • The four ranges cover similar shares of the total branch length (about 30% "B", 26% "AB", 25% "A" and 20% "BC").

  • A moderate number of changes of range: 10 of the 58 branches include a change of range (no branch has more than 3 pieces).

  • Each range is found in 5 to 10 of the 30 tips.

Usage

data(toy_simmap_ranges)

Format

An object of classes "simmap" and "phylo" (see phytools::make.simmap()), with the same tips, topology and branch lengths as phylograftR::toy_backbone, and the additional elements $maps (for each branch, the duration spent in each range, from the rootward node to the tipward node), $mapped.edge (total duration per range and branch), $node.states and $states (ranges of the nodes and tips).

Details

Events represented in the map, with the syntax of BioGeoBEARS.

Anagenetic changes (along the branches, 12 in total):

  • 8 "d" (range expansion, gain of one area): 5 "A" -> "AB" and 3 "B" -> "BC".

  • 4 "e" (range contraction, loss of one area): 3 "AB" -> "A" and 1 "AB" -> "B".

Cladogenetic events (at the 29 nodes, from the range of the lineage above the node and the ranges at the start of the two descendant branches):

  • 5 "s" (subset sympatry), such as (AB) -> (AB), (A): one descendant keeps the widespread range, the other starts in a single area within it. They are the events that are produced by the grafting functions when a taxon inherits an allowed range smaller than the range of the lineage it is grafted on (subset sympatric speciation, see phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()).

  • 1 "v" (vicariance), (AB) -> (A), (B): the widespread range is split between the two descendants.

  • 13 "y" (narrow sympatry): both descendants inherit the single-area range of the lineage, such as (A) -> (A), (A).

  • 10 nodes where both descendants inherit the same widespread range (widespread sympatry): (AB) -> (AB), (AB) or (BC) -> (BC), (BC) (allowed in BAYAREALIKE-type models, but not in DEC).

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges for the list of missing taxa to graft, with associated allowed biogeographic ranges.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa within a target clade based on geographic ranges, using this dataset.

Examples

# Import the data
data(toy_simmap_ranges)

# Plot the map
range_colors <- c(A = "gold", B = "dodgerblue", AB = "limegreen", BC = "firebrick2")
phytools::plotSimmap(toy_simmap_ranges, colors = range_colors, fsize = 0.7, ftype = "i")


# Duration spent in each range (sum on all the branches)
colSums(toy_simmap_ranges$mapped.edge)
#>       AB        B        A       BC 
#> 62.15758 71.59366 59.53341 48.76147
